narratives.Description: feat(doctor,ritual): detect when a newer published release is available at session start (latest-release comparison, not just pinned-ref movement)
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

At consumer session-start, Deft should tell the operator when a **newer published release** of the framework is available. Today the `payload-staleness` check in `scripts/doctor.py` only detects when the **pinned ref has moved** -- it does **not** detect that a newer release/tag exists. A consumer pinned to an immutable release tag is never told a newer version shipped.

## Current state (what already works)

`scripts/doctor.py` `payload-staleness` check (#1339 / #1409 / #1384 / #1427):

- Reads the install `VERSION` manifest's pinned `ref`/`tag` + `sha`.
- Resolves the **remote** sha via `git ls-remote origin <ref>` (no fetch, best-effort, 15s timeout).
- If installed sha != remote sha, emits a warning + the canonical headless upgrader `deft-install --yes --upgrade --repo-root . --json`.

This is already wired into the session-start ritual (the gated tier `task verify:session-ritual --tier=gated` lazily records `task doctor`; the installer also runs `doctor.py --session --json` at the end of every run).

## The gap

The comparison is against the remote sha **of the ref the install is pinned to**. If the manifest pins an immutable release tag (e.g. `v0.50.0`), `git ls-remote origin v0.50.0` returns the same sha forever, so the check reports **"current"** even after `v0.51.0` ships.

It answers *"has my pinned branch moved?"* -- not *"is there a newer version available?"*. The latter is what a normal consumer actually wants at startup.

## Proposed approach

- Add a check (extend `payload-staleness` or add a sibling `release-available` check) that compares the installed version against the **latest published release**:
  - Resolve latest via `git ls-remote --tags --refs origin` (highest SemVer tag) or `gh api repos/deftai/directive/releases/latest` (`tagName`) when `gh` is available.
  - Compare against the installed version/tag from the `VERSION` manifest.
  - When the latest release is newer, emit an informational nudge + the canonical upgrade command (reuse the existing #1409 one-liner).
- Keep it **best-effort / non-fatal**: skip cleanly on no network, no `gh`, no origin, or inside the framework repo itself (mirror the existing skip ladder).
- Respect SemVer pre-release tags (do not nudge a stable install toward an `-rc`/`-beta`/`-alpha` tag) -- ties into #425's pre-release flagging.
- Surface through the same session-ritual / `task doctor --session` path so consumers see it at startup without a new step.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a consumer pinned to release tag `vX.Y.Z`, when `vX.Y.(Z+1)` (or higher) is published, `task doctor` / session ritual surfaces a "newer release available" nudge with the upgrade command.
- [ ] When the install is already on the latest release, no nudge is emitted.
- [ ] Pre-release tags do not trigger a nudge for stable installs.
- [ ] Check is non-fatal and skips cleanly with no network / no `gh` / no origin / inside the framework repo.
- [ ] Regression test covering: newer-release-available, already-latest, pre-release-skip, and offline-skip.

## Related

- #1604 -- Upgrade workflow should carry framework updates through default-branch release handoff (upgrade mechanics)
- #1411 -- "Stuck on an old Deft version?" (support/triage)
- #1157 -- greenfield / migrate:vbrief path leaves .deft-version unstamped (version provenance)
- #425 -- flag SemVer pre-release tags (pre-release detection logic to reuse)

## Source

Discovered while auditing the session-start ritual's version-awareness on 2026-06-17. The existing `payload-staleness` check covers pinned-ref movement but not latest-release availability.

---

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-06-17T12:50:20Z)

Labeled **Upgrade Blocker** in the *adoption* sense: the upgrade mechanism itself works, but consumers pinned to an immutable release tag get no signal that a newer version exists, so they never initiate the upgrade. Silent staleness is the most common real-world reason a consumer stays behind -- distinct from the mechanical upgrade-path breakages (#1425, #1433, #1437, #1440, #1441, #1604) that also carry this label.

### Comment by @rockbox37 (2026-07-13T19:11:59Z)

Follow-on filed: #2488 — `feat(triage,doctor): staleness "tickler" — offer Directive + xBRIEF upgrade at safe idle points before drift compounds`.

#2488 is designed to **consume** this issue's detection substrate rather than reimplement it. Where #1692 answers *"is a newer release available?"* and surfaces a passive line at session start, #2488 adds:

- an **interactive, opt-in prompt** ("upgrade now?") instead of only an informational notice;
- **timing for work-stopped/idle points** (clean tree, no `running` story, never mid-swarm) rather than session start only;
- a second staleness axis for the **xBRIEF schema version** (offering `deft migrate:xbrief`), not just the Directive payload;
- **escalation as drift compounds**, to fight the deferral doom-loop.

If this lands first, #2488 builds directly on the `release-available` comparison here.
